newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia puts more aircraft on Cambodia standby.
newsitem.headline: Australia puts more aircraft on Cambodia standby.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday placed three more military aircraft on standby for a possible evacuation of Australians from strife-torn Cambodia.

A defence department spokeswoman said three more C130 Hercules transport planes had been sent to the northern Australian town of Darwin, in addition to two already on standby at the Butterworth air base in Malaysia.
"They will go to Darwin and wait to see what the government will do," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"They are close to where the action is if we need to do something with them," she said.
But a government spokesman said that at this stage it did not seem likely that an evacuation of Australians, Canadians and New Zealanders from Cambodia was necessary.
The Southeast Asian nation was thrown into turmoil at the weekend when Second Prime Minister Hun Sen took control of the capital Phnom Penh.

Fighting between Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party and forces loyal to First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh appeared to have abated since Monday, although parts of Phnom Penh remained violent as troops celebrated their victory with looting.
A spokesman for Foreign Minister Alexander Downer confirmed that the situation in the capital remained calm and said it was hoped that commercial flights would resume later this week.
"There's basically the belief that commercial flights may resume later this week and that would be the way to go," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said the military aircraft were "just a standby measure". There are around 500 Australians believed to be in Cambodia.
